results.title: Model monitoring for ML in production: a comprehensive ...
results.content: * **Model monitoring** includes tracking metrics related to model quality (e.g., accuracy, precision, etc.), data and prediction drift, data quality, model bias, and fairness. > **TL;DR:** Production ML monitoring tracks the quality of the model performance on live data. Model monitoring tracks the quality of individual ML models, which may involve checking their input data quality. There is some overlap between data and model quality monitoring – especially at the implementation level when it comes to specific tests and metrics you can run, such as tracking missing data. Model monitoring covers various metrics and aspects of ML model quality on top of the quality of the input data – from model accuracy to prediction bias. Since an ML-based service goes beyond just the ML model, the ML system quality has several facets: software, data, model, and business KPIs. Each involves monitoring different groups of metrics. You can use data drift analysis as a monitoring and debugging technique for production ML models to evaluate if the model still operates in a familiar environment.

results.title: mapping the diffusion of misinformation in algorithmic ...
results.content: Unlike the diffusion of beneficial ideas, the diffusion of misinformation is often driven by cognitive biases, emotional triggers, and the amplification effects of algorithmic platforms (Buchanan 2020 Why do people spread false information online? Prior studies have explored various factors contributing to the spread of misinformation, including human cognitive biases, platform algorithms, and social dynamics (e.g., Roozenbeek and van der Linden 2024 The psychology of misinformation. It informs the design of the empirical protocol (e.g., interview questions probing novelty perception, emotional engagement, and perceived credibility), shapes the analytic coding schema (e.g., mapping participant narratives to adopter profiles), and underpins the theoretical modeling of misinformation diffusion curves. The diffusion curve of misinformation follows a steep s-curve, illustrating the rapid spread of false information within a network, driven primarily by algorithmic amplification on social media platforms. By outlining the phases of misinformation diffusion and identifying mechanisms, such as cognitive alignment, emotional salience, social reinforcement, and algorithmic amplification, the study contributes to ongoing efforts to conceptualize misinformation as a dynamic socio-technical process.
